### Supplementary Table 3 | Bimetallic surface layers of the ammonia screen

From `analysis/nh3_alloy_extension_2026_10_05/nh3_1_2/summary.json`. 1,796 surfaces (5,696 N* sites) were fetched; 101 contain Tc, which has no market price, and are not costed; the 1,695 costed surfaces are 372 transition-metal, 540 with a group 3–5 element and 783 with an sp metal. Layers are cumulative. Feasible: inside the 90 m³ bed limit. Surfaces below Fe (11.52 USD/t NH₃) are listed in order of cost for the global bridge (slope 0.845, R² 0.973, RMS 0.22 eV over 14 pure metals) and with their cost (USD/t) for the element-anchored bridge. Pruned: candidates ruled out by the descriptor-only lower bound before the full 14,510-state optimization (`provenance/nh3_final_1_2/source_harness/outputs/nh3_final_1_2_20261013/results.json`); false prunes: pruned candidates whose full optimization falls below Fe.

### Supplementary Table 4a | Deviations of the ammonia model from industrial plants

The 64 comparisons of the ammonia model with industrial synthesis loops and converters, by quantity (`analysis/nh3_keestra_consolidation_2026_10_20/error_summary.csv`; every item in Supplementary Table 4c). Deviation: (model − industrial)/industrial for point values, the difference in °C for temperatures, and the distance to the nearer edge for published ranges (0 inside the range). Typical: median absolute deviation of the items of a quantity; largest: their maximum, with the item. Within tolerance: items whose deviation lies within the tolerance listed with them (33 of 64). Four logical items (Fe/Ru choice and staging) have no numeric deviation. Component: the model component perturbed in Supplementary Table 4b for the failing items of the quantity. Converter items use the measured rate laws of fused iron (Keestra et al. Model 3, Topsoe KM1R activity, fitted 1–324 bar) and Ru/C (Rossetti et al., 50–100 bar) inside their fitted pressure ranges. C08 and C10 keep their registered scores.

### Supplementary Table 4b | The Fe–Ru order under the benchmark deviations

Catalyst-dependent cost difference at the reoptimized optima, US dollars per tonne of NH₃ (positive: Fe cheaper), with each component perturbed at the upgraded magnitudes of Supplementary Table 4a (`analysis/nh3_keestra_consolidation_2026_10_20/perturbation_magnitudes.json`). Descriptor results: `analysis/nh3_keestra_consolidation_2026_10_20/perturbation_descriptor_results.csv` and `analysis/nh3_keestra_consolidation_2026_10_20/perturbation_descriptor_summary.json`; measured results: `analysis/nh3_keestra_consolidation_2026_10_20/perturbation_results.csv` and `analysis/nh3_keestra_consolidation_2026_10_20/perturbation_summary.json`. Typical and largest: median and maximum component-error magnitudes; largest at plant conditions: the largest plant-condition bed-volume error. Each perturbation is applied in both directions (28 single cases), with catalyst-specific reoptimization and a 90 m³ bed limit. Descriptor: the canonical model. Measured columns use Keestra et al. Model 3 for fused iron (Topsoe KM1R activity, 1–324 bar) and Rossetti et al. for Ru/C (50–100 bar), with both catalysts restricted to their fitted pressure ranges. Bulk benchmark uses the benchmark catalyst-amount formulation; supported Ru/C uses its own bed, 95.55% metal recovery and inventory financing at 0 or 12%/y. The KAAP-type loop fixes 90 bar and −20 °C separation. Single cases that reverse each column's baseline order (including loss of feasibility): Ru − Fe, descriptor 0/28, Os − Fe, descriptor 0/28, Ru − Fe, measured, bulk benchmark 2/28, Ru/C − Fe, measured, benchmark loop, 0%/y 1/28, Ru/C − Fe, measured, benchmark loop, 12%/y 3/28, Ru/C − Fe, measured, KAAP-type loop, 0%/y 1/28, Ru/C − Fe, measured, KAAP-type loop, 12%/y 5/28. Combinations: every component at the same magnitude; towards Ru, the direction that alone narrows the gap most; least favourable, the smallest gap over all 2⁵ sign combinations and both catalyst-amount forms (64 corners per magnitude). No feasible Fe or Ru/C denotes loss of that catalyst's feasible states, rather than a finite cost margin; no feasible state denotes neither feasible.

### Supplementary Table 4c | The 64 benchmark items

Every item of Supplementary Table 4a (`analysis/nh3_keestra_consolidation_2026_10_20/error_table.csv`). Industrial: the published value or range; logical items compare a decision (yes or no) or a threshold. Deviation: as in Supplementary Table 4a, signed (negative: model low). Converter items use the measured rate laws of fused iron (Keestra et al. Model 3, Topsoe KM1R activity, fitted 1–324 bar) and Ru/C (Rossetti et al., 50–100 bar) inside their fitted pressure ranges. C08 and C10 keep their registered scores.

### Supplementary Table 5a | Leave-one-out validation of the Fe terrace-to-step bridge

Terrace and observed step-site N formation energies of the 14 metals with both values in Dataset S1, and the step value predicted with that metal left out, from `analysis/fe_bridge_backward_2026_09_29/fe_bridge_loo.csv`; the Fe terrace value is the Dataset S1 entry used by `analysis/nh3_alloy_extension_2026_10_05/run_alloy_chain.py`. Statistics in Supplementary Table 5b are recomputed from these rows.

### Supplementary Table 5b | Statistics of the Fe terrace-to-step bridge

Ordinary least squares on Supplementary Table 5a. The global 14-metal fit is the relation used for Fe in the model; its residual standard error is the Fe descriptor uncertainty of the descriptor Monte Carlo analysis. The strong-binding branch (terrace *E*_{N} ≤ −0.5 eV: Mo, Os, Re, Ru, W) is a sensitivity check and is not used in the model. Prediction interval: Student t with n − 2 degrees of freedom.

### Supplementary Table 6b | Plant metrics of the model loop at each reference operating point

Model values from `analysis/meoh_plant_benchmark_2026_10_06/reconciliation_plant.csv` (recycled CO, central RWGS rule). Columns: M1, anchor one-step (calibration point); M2, anchor three-step inputs (out-of-sample design); M3, canonical economic optimum, 5 wt% Re 200 C, 2 % purge; M4, canonical optimum at own purge, 1 wt% Re 200 C, 0.5 % purge; M5, at Lurgi CO2-pilot conditions (80 bar, X 0.40, CE 95.25 %); M6, at Gonzalez-Garay conditions (50 bar, X 0.141, CE 91.5 %); M7, at Perez-Fortes 2016 point (76 bar, X 0.2197, 1 % purge, 44.5 t); M8, at Van-Dal 2013 point (75.7 bar, X 0.33, 1 % purge, 44.5 t); M9, at Szima 2018 point (80 bar, X 0.30, 1 % purge); M10, at Nyari 2022 Slotboom point (fitted to RR 2.89, CE 0.937); M11, at Nyari 2022 VD point (fitted to RR 7.67, CE 0.896); M12, at Nieminen 2019 gas-phase point (50 bar, X 0.203, S 0.961). Catalyst lifetime (y): 3 (in constant residual; no inventory term) in every case. Reference values for each metric are in Supplementary Table 6c.

### Supplementary Table 6d | Cost at each study's own prices, scale and finance

From `analysis/meoh_plant_benchmark_2026_10_06/reconciliation_cost.csv` (€/t methanol unless stated). Like-for-like: feed, compression electricity, catalyst replacement and capital annuity at the study's own rate, plus the study's own fixed O&M; for Pérez-Fortes 2016 the reference is its NPV = 0 break-even methanol price (production cost plus capital recovery), not a production cost. ### Supplementary Table 7 | The 161 methanol comparison groups and the 81 of the primary analysis

One row per comparison group of the all-entries cohort (entries of one paper at the same pressure, H₂/CO₂ ratio and space velocity, plot readings included), from `analysis/meoh_field_pooled_2026_10_15/robustness/group_ledger/group_ledger.csv`; counts checked against `analysis/meoh_field_pooled_2026_10_15/robustness/group_ledger/ledger_summary.json`. Entries: all entries of the group / entries with printed conversion and selectivities. The same grouping rule applied to printed values alone keeps 81 groups (632 entries, 50 papers); 33 groups come from 22 papers without printed values and 47 have fewer than two printed entries (30 with none, 17 with one). Verdict columns: whether the space-time-yield leader of the group is not its plant-cost leader, with the regret where it is not; inlet limit, CO, methane and N₂ at most 6.86% of the reactor inlet (primary); no limit, the loop without it. Printed values: the primary analysis, from `analysis/meoh_field_pooled_2026_10_15/groups_S6.csv` and `analysis/meoh_field_pooled_2026_10_15/groups_S5.csv`. Set: first or second extraction. All entries: the sensitivity with plot readings, from the ledger; under the inlet limit one group keeps fewer than two entries that can meet the limit (–).

### Supplementary Table 8a | Errors in the curated reference data confirmed against the papers

One row per source paper with a confirmed error. A root cause is one mechanism in one source paper; error rules group the cells of one paper, field and cause; rows are records of conditions the paper did not test. TheMeCat stores STY as yield × GHSV × CO₂ fraction × 32.04/24.05 rather than the printed value, so a derived STY is counted only with the input error it inherits (last column). Per-cell old value, printed value, dataset row and locator: `analysis/verify_2026_10_08/errata_cells_audit.csv`; rules and classes: `analysis/verify_2026_10_08/errata_adjudication.csv`. Total: 26 root causes, 45 error rules, 169 value cells and 8 rows; 24 further STY cells derived from them.

### Supplementary Table 8b | Differences of definition and minor differences, not counted as errors

Differences between curated and printed values that are not errors of the curated data. Definition: the paper's printed STY differs from the STY that TheMeCat derives from yield and GHSV, or the paper prints STY on bases it does not reconcile (10.1021/acsami.1c05586). Minor: at most 2 % and at most one unit of the last printed digit. Total: definition 139 cells, minor 13 cells. The printed values are used for scoring in both cases.

### Supplementary Table 9 | Source types and accuracy of 100 sampled extracted values

From `analysis/extraction_ledger_2026_10_21/summary.json` and `analysis/extraction_ledger_2026_10_21/ledger_100.csv` (one row per value), built by `analysis/extraction_ledger_2026_10_21/build_ledger.py` from the source evidence of the 100-value sample. Errors: #40 (10.1038/s41467-019-11349-9): conversion printed for the 500 h stability test (text, Fig. 6) attached to the Table 2 entry; Table 2 has no conversion column; #99 (10.1016/j.jcat.2012.05.020): methanol formation rate printed in µmol per gram of catalyst per minute recorded as a printed STY without the paper's metric name; the value converts to the same STY. Removing #40 changes no catalyst-level comparison; the point-level count of the inlet-limited loop goes from 50 to 51 of 81. #99 converts to the STY the model uses (0.000577 g per g catalyst per h). Plot-read rows: strict tolerance against the curated datasets (`agent/extraction/eval/field_accuracy_by_source.csv`, main-text and SI plots pooled).
